headline: Massachusetts gov says Dems want ‘a uniter and a fighter’ for 2028
author: Lisa Kashinsky

paragraphs.text: Democrats want fighters. Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey believes they want healers, too.

Healey, a Democrat who easily won a second term in the deep-blue state earlier this month, told POLITICO on Thursday that she’d like to see her party’s next presidential nominee show “decency” and “humanity.”

“It’s really important that we have leaders who genuinely see people, understand their situation. If you don't see people, if you don't understand people, you're never going to be able to deliver for them,” Healey said during an interview at the POLITICO Pub on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Deer Valley, Utah.
“Having leaders who have that, and who have a strong moral compass, I think that's really important,” she told POLITICO’s Adam Wren.

Healey suggested the midterms offered a “resetting” as the nation moves toward a post-Donald Trump era. Pressed on whether it’s more important for Democrats to nominate a fighter or a healer, Healey — who burnished her national profile as a hard-charging state attorney general who sued the first Trump administration dozens of times and urged Democrats to more aggressively oppose his second — insisted good leaders can do both.
“You can be a uniter and a fighter; you can be a fighter and a healer,” she said.

It’s a debate that’s already driving the earliest stages of Democrats’ shadow 2028 primary as the party’s rising stars try to discern whether voters who powered their midterm wave want a brawler or a uniter after candidates of both stripes won difficult races.
Healey ruled out a 2028 presidential bid of her own on Thursday. And she deflected when asked whether Democrats should nominate a governor.

But the Massachusetts governor, who has close relationships with several likely contenders and routinely hits the campaign trail for Democrats in the early primary state of New Hampshire, could play a role in shaping the primary.
